articles.title: NFL looking into line judge appearing to curse out Cardinals’ Trey McBride during game
articles.summary: Incident came after tight end appealed non-call. Players’ union says incident was unacceptable. The NFL is looking into the circumstances of an official swearing at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during the team’s loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, league spokesperson Brian McCarthy…
body: Line judge Jeff Seeman was caught on camera cursing at McBride, who appeared to laugh when he realized a camera had caught the incident. The interaction drew the ire of NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter, a retired offensive lineman who played eight seasons in the league.

“This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable,” Tretter said in a social media post which included a clip of the incident. “Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard.”
The NFL Referees Association did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

The incident took place with just under five minutes left after officials did not call a penalty on New York’s Dru Phillips on a crucial third down, which the Cardinals did not convert. McBride questioned the call and Seeman appeared to respond to his appeal by saying “fuck you”. Arizona punted and the Giants went on to win the game 36-24. McBride did not address the incident in his postgame comments.

articles.title: Australia’s Marnus Labuschagne set for South Africa Test after first ton in 11 months
articles.summary: Batter makes 111 against Cricket South Africa Invitation XI. Three-match Test series starts in Durban on Friday. The indefatigable Marnus Labuschagne has responded to all the hand-wringing over whether he merits a place in Australia’s Test future by just doing what he likes doing best – scoring…
body: After a difficult year, the under-pressure 32-year-old chose the most timely moment to score his first century in any form of cricket for 11 months in Potchefstroom, just five days before Australia play their first Test in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.

Former skipper Ricky Ponting has led the chorus that Labuschagne’s Australia place has become “untenable” after three years and 43 Tests without a Test ton, capped by three failures in the recent Bangladesh series.

Yet the South Africa-born batter looks sure to fill the No 3 spot once more in the first Test that starts in Durban on Friday after his swift century against a modest Cricket South Africa Invitation XI attack on Sunday.

Labuschagne was largely untroubled as he raced to a 76-ball ton, going on to 111 from 89, decorated with 19 fours, before retiring to let his colleagues also get in some batting practice on the final day of the two-day warm-up match.

articles.title: Clàudia Pina hits four as Barcelona score seven goals to demolish Real Madrid
articles.summary: Barcelona 7-0 Real Madrid. Lead at the top stretched to five points. Clàudia Pina smashed in four goals as Barcelona demolished Real Madrid 7-0 to earn a five point lead at the top of Liga F on Sunday over their rivals.
body: The 25-year-old Spain international was in lethal form in front of goal as a dominant Barça won the Clásico battle with ease at the Camp Nou in front of over 40,000 fans, continuing their perfect start to the campaign. The match was pushed back by two hours after torrential rain in the Catalonia region over the weekend.
Pina put Barcelona, who have won the league seven seasons running, in the driving seat after just four minutes with a neat finish after breezing into the area.

The Catalan side controlled the ball and Madrid found it hard to pry it away from them, although managed to fend them off until Pina’s second in the 28th minute, the first of three goals in around five minutes.
Ewa Pajor’s shot was blocked and Pina polished off the rebound, completing her hat-trick a few minutes later by blasting into the top corner.

articles.title: No other team should go through this - Hallgrimsson
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says he is "delighted" this most trying of international windows is over and hopes "no national team to go through what we have gone through over the last two weeks".
body: With four games played - just one on Irish soil - and about 5,000 miles travelled, Sunday's behind-closed-doors 1-1 draw against Israel in the Serbian town of Backa Topola brought the curtain down on two weeks that have taken their toll.

That his side took the field against Israel this week, and in last week's 3-0 victory in Debrecen, came under scrutiny and fire with the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine's 'Stop The Game' campaign for a boycott because of the Israel-Gaza war.

That pressure ramped up before last Sunday's victory in Hungary with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for those fixtures because he felt "it would be wrong to participate". A vote held between the remaining players on whether to procced with the Israel games featured on a chaotic day.
On the eve of Sunday's match, Hallgrimsson's news conference was cut short when an Israeli reporter made accusations that some Irish players made racist comments in their victory last week.

articles.title: Bellamy bemoans new schedule after Denmark loss
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy suggests the new four-match international window has counted against Wales after Sunday's Nations League defeat against Denmark.
body: His side failed to build on Thursday's win over Norway as they were deservedly beaten thanks to a second-half Rasmus Hojlund penalty.
It was a third loss in four games played inside 10 days as part of the newly elongated international break.
Head coach Bellamy said his injury-hit squad paid the price for the heavy workload he feels benefits the bigger nations and "puts a real stress" on countries like Wales.
"Physically, I completely agree with the ones who don't like [the new window]. It makes no sense," he added.

articles.title: 49ers game grades: Big-time defense, game-plan synergy help beat the Broncos
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers faced perhaps their toughest opponent since their takedown of the Los Angeles Rams in the season opener, on one of the hottest days ever at Levi's Stadium.
body: Quarterback Brock Purdy remained unsacked and delivered two touchdown passes, both in the second half, with George Kittle 's breakaway rumble for 56 yards into the end zone in the fourth quarter being the coup de grace. But after a slow start in the first half, the running game and the offensive line deserves some love for what it unglamourously delivered on a steamy Sunday, and not just Christian McCaffrey punching it into the end zone with 8:52 left or Deebo Samuel 's pair of chunk plays from scrimmage. By grinding out 140 yards on 35 carries, the injury-riddled defense had to spend that much less time on the field, which paid dividends.

articles.title: Humphries wins Grand Prix to end barren spell
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries ends a 16-month wait for a PDC major trophy with a stunning 6-4 victory over Gerwyn Price in the World Grand Prix final.
body: Humphries, 31, was at the top of the sport two years ago but has found his dominance superseded by Luke Littler and had failed to taste major success since winning the Premier League in May 2025.

A ranking title had eluded him since claiming the Masters in February last year, but he showed his class and an abundance of character to lift the title at the unique 'double-in, double-out' tournament in Leicester.
The second seed, who was in a record-breaking fourth successive World Grand Prix final, trailed Price 3-0 but won four sets on the spin to take control.
Price levelled but Humphries broke in the deciding leg of set five and then won three straight legs to be crowned champion.

articles.title: Mardle: Humphries can do it against anyone from any position
articles.summary: Sky Sports Darts pundit Wayne Mardle reflects on Luke Humphries becoming a two-time World Grand Prix champion after 'Cool Hand' rallied from 3-0 down against Gerwyn Price in the final to triumph 6-4 at the double-start event…
body: I may be wrong but, a few years ago, I don't think Luke would have hung in a game like that to win it.
That was sheer belief: guts and determination knowing that you can do it - and he can do it against anyone from any position.

When you have won before, and Luke has done many, many times and in many, many ways, there is that belief of, 'I'm under pressure but let's just see as I know if I settle down my game can win', rather than 'oh no, I am going to get beat or get embarrassed 6-0'.
He played his game and he won. I am not saying it's that simple but sometimes you have to simplify it.

body: Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.
Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O'Flaherty produced the match's pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try.

articles.title: Eagles' offense completely collapses vs. Rams: Who's to blame and what needs to change
articles.summary: The offensive meltdown after having the chance to deliver the knockout punch to Los Angeles highlights an uncomfortable truth in Philadelphia
body: The Philadelphia Eagles ' 24-20 collapse at home against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 on Sunday is a five-alarm fire for the back-to-back NFC East division champions.

Philadelphia had Los Angeles on the proverbial ropes. The Eagles led 20-10, and they had the ball on the two, just a couple of yards from scoring a touchdown that would land the knockout punch and put the game entirely out of reach with under eight minutes to play. At that moment, the NFL's Next Gen Stats assessed the Rams had a win probability as minuscule as 3.2%.

But Los Angeles stuffed quarterback Jalen Hurts on Philadelphia's famed "Tush Push" play before he threw incomplete on fourth-and-goal to force a turnover on downs. From that moment on, on their final two drives, the Eagles' offense lost a combined 14 yards. The Rams mounted consecutive, 10-play touchdown drives capped by rushing touchdowns from running back Kyren Williams.
